policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders a singular participle with a feminine-singular object suffix: 'whosoever heareth of it', the 'it' being the evil Jehovah brings upon Jerusalem and Judah, and the hearer singular ('his ears'). That is the qere שֹׁמְעָהּ, a singular participle plus 3fs suffix. The ketiv שמעיו is a plural participle with a 3ms suffix ('his hearers' / those who hear him), which supplies neither the singular subject nor the 'of it' the ASV prints. No ASV note is mapped to this unit; the wording alone distinguishes the reading.
